# input: # No number agreement, and no space between the number and the unit — on
# input or on output, which is what makes the round trip hold. The separators
# are English's: "," for groups, "." for the decimal.
# The katakana names read and the Latin symbols print, which is a claim about
# register and not about the lexer. Seven of the nine words survive ICU's
# Japanese dictionary whole; テラバイト and キビバイト come back cut in two, so
# spelling the decimal family would print 「1.5ギガバイト」 beside 「2TB」 —
# one kind in two registers, with the choice made by a dictionary.
# The myriad. Japanese counts in ten-thousands, so 万 is a magnitude word in
# its own right and 一万 is one of them, not ten of a thousand.
# を and から are case particles, glued to the word they mark rather than
# standing between words, and both introduce a conversion target.
# The word operators do stand alone and take whitespace. かける and 掛ける are
# the same operator in two orthographies, kana and kanji.
